chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Ibn Mahbub from Khalid ibn Jarir from Abu al-Rabīʿ said:

I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about a man who traveled to Mecca and had a flock of pigeons in his house, which were accustomed to wild birds that joined them. He said: 'His family should observe the quantity [of food] until the time they believe he will enter the state of ihram, and they should not expose those birds to disturbance nor startle them, and they should feed them until the Day of Sacrifice, and their owner becomes free from his ihram.'

key_terms.إِحْرَامٌ: State of consecration for Hajj or Umrah

ai.seo_question: What should be done with pigeons left at home when a man goes for Hajj?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) provides a practical solution for the 'kaffarah' (expiation) of a pilgrim who leaves behind domestic pigeons that have mingled with wild game birds. The ruling emphasizes that the family must feed and keep the birds undisturbed until the pilgrim completes his rites and returns from Ihram, effectively treating the birds as a temporary extension of the pilgrim's state of consecration. This highlights the Shia juristic principle of managing accidental violations through custodial care rather than immediate slaughter or release.
